record.paper_title: Some Results and Open Problems on the Controllability of Linear and Semilinear Heat Equations
record.context_brief: Sharp observability constants for the constant-coefficient heat equation
record.original_question: Let Ω be a bounded smooth domain, let ω be a nonempty open subset of Ω, and consider the linear heat equation φ_t − Δφ = 0 in Ω × (0,T) with homogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions on ∂Ω × (0,T). There exist constants γ > 0 and C > 0 such that the weighted observability inequality ∫_0^T∫_Ω e^{-γ/t} φ(x,t)^2 dx dt ≤ C ∫_0^T∫_ω φ(x,t)^2 dx dt holds for every solution, and the analogous inequality also makes sense on the infinite time interval because the L²-norm of solutions decays exponentially. Determine the best possible constant γ in these observability inequalities, in particular in the infinite-time version ∫_0^∞∫_Ω e^{-γ/t} φ(x,t)^2 dx dt ≤ C ∫_0^∞∫_ω φ(x,t)^2 dx dt, and decide whether the lower bound γ ≥ sup_{B(x_0,p)⊂Ω\ω} p^2/4 is sharp, especially in radially symmetric geometries.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be a bounded domain with smooth boundary, and let $\omega\subset\Omega$ be a nonempty open subset. For $T\in(0,\infty]$, consider the linear heat equation
$$\varphi_t-\Delta\varphi=0\quad\text{in }\Omega\times(0,T),\qquad \varphi=0\quad\text{on }\partial\Omega\times(0,T),$$
with initial data $\varphi(\cdot,0)\in L^2(\Omega)$. It is known that there exist constants $\gamma>0$ and $C=C(\gamma)>0$ such that the weighted observability inequality
$$\int_0^T\!\!\int_\Omega e^{-\gamma/t}\,\varphi(x,t)^2\,dx\,dt\;\le\;C\int_0^T\!\!\int_\omega \varphi(x,t)^2\,dx\,dt$$
holds for every solution $\varphi$. Because solutions decay exponentially in $L^2(\Omega)$, the inequality also makes sense with $T=\infty$:
$$\int_0^\infty\!\!\int_\Omega e^{-\gamma/t}\,\varphi(x,t)^2\,dx\,dt\;\le\;C\int_0^\infty\!\!\int_\omega \varphi(x,t)^2\,dx\,dt.$$
Determine the best (smallest) admissible constant $\gamma>0$ for which such an inequality holds, in particular in the infinite-time version. Furthermore, given the geometric lower bound
$$\gamma\;\ge\;\sup\{\,\rho^2/4\;:\;B(x_0,\rho)\subset\Omega\setminus\omega\,\},$$
decide whether this lower bound is attained (i.e., is sharp), especially when $(\Omega,\omega)$ is radially symmetric.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent work by Ervedoza and Zuazua ("Sharp Observability Estimates for Heat Equations", Arch. Ration. Mech. Anal. 202 (2011), 975–1017) develops transmutation techniques that yield observability estimates for the heat equation derived from those for the wave equation, and the authors state that their estimates are sharp in one space dimension and in multi-dimensional radially symmetric situations, providing partial confirmation of the conjectured sharpness of the geometric lower bound γ ≥ sup ρ²/4. However, a full characterization of the optimal γ for general bounded smooth domains and observation subsets does not appear to have been established.

status_evidence.title: Sharp Observability Estimates for Heat Equations (Ervedoza–Zuazua)
status_evidence.snippet: New estimates for the cost of observability of heat equations... shown to be sharp in some cases, particularly in one space dimension and in the multi-dimensional radially symmetric case.
status_evidence.claim: Provides sharp observability estimates in 1D and radially symmetric multi-D, partially confirming sharpness of the geometric lower bound.

status_evidence.title: Sharp observability estimates for heat equations (preprint)
status_evidence.snippet: Transmutation techniques yielding sharp constants relating wave and heat observability; section on exponential observability cost in finite time.
status_evidence.claim: Addresses the explicit dependence of the observability constant on the geometry, with sharpness in symmetric settings.
